packages.label: עֹרֶף וְלוּז — הַמָּקוֹם הַנֶּחְבָּא
packages.label_en: The Nape and the Luz — The Hidden Place
packages.reason: All these concepts designate the same anatomical-spiritual zone: the back-of-neck/nape region and its encoded names. עֹרֶף (nape) is the location of the Luz bone; לוּז is both the bone's name and the city adjacent to Beit El; קָדְקֹד (crown/skull) has the same gematria as 'נַחֲמוּ נַחֲמוּ' (two times 'be comforted') and is a bechina of the nape; שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים נַחֲמוּ equals קָדְקֹד by gematria and thus equals ערף; כְּתֵפָיו (shoulders — Benjamin's blessing) is cited alongside קָדְקֹד (Joseph's blessing) as the same Luz dimension; שַׁבַּת נַחֲמוּ has gematria ש״נ = ש״נ = the same letters as ערף, making it a bechina of ערף. These are structural neutral objects (body-part names, scriptural terms) that all point to the same hidden-yet-imperishable dimension. The pair אֱגוֹזִים הַנִּקְרָאִים לוּזִים — לֵאָה is merged here because: the text explicitly states the Luz-nuts 'hint at the bechina of Leah who is in the nape (עֹרֶף),' making both the nuts and Leah expressions of the same נֶפֶשׁ רִאשׁוֹנָה / ערף zone.

merge_notes.reason: This isolated pair was a separate 2-node component. The proof text states explicitly: 'אֱגוֹזִים הַנִּקְרָאִים לוּזִים, הֵם רוֹמְזִים לִבְחִינַת לֵאָה שֶׁהִיא בָּעֹרֶף' — the Luz-nuts hint at Leah who is in the nape (ערף). Both the nuts and Leah are expressions of the same ערף / Luz-zone dimension, identical in essential nature to the Luz-nape cluster. Merged into Package 1 rather than Package 2 because Leah's nature here is as the first (ראשונה), the hidden preliminary zone, not the resurrection-consolation theme of Package 2.

packages.label: עֶצֶם לוּז וְנֶחָמָה — הַגּוּף הַנִּצְחִי
packages.label_en: The Luz Bone and Consolation — The Eternal Body
packages.reason: These concepts all express the same essential reality: latent indestructibility and the promise of future renewal. עֶצֶם לוּז is the imperishable bone in the human nape from which the body will be rebuilt at resurrection; אִילַן לוּז is the Luz tree whose 21-day cycle corresponds to the Three Weeks of mourning and the egg's incubation period, embodying the same pattern of survival-through-concealment; שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׁבוּעוֹת שֶׁהֵם עֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד יוֹם שֶׁבֵּין הַמְּצָרִים is the 21-day mourning period, identical in its numeric structure to the Luz tree's cycle; בֵּיצָה (egg) shares the same 21-day period of completion (a hen hatches in 21 days), making it a parallel expression of the same pattern of hidden development leading to emergence; עִקַּר נֶחָמוֹתֵינוּ (the essence of our consolation) is identified explicitly as the Luz bone itself — resurrection is the ultimate consolation. The pair בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ — בֵּית אֵל is merged here because: the Beit HaMikdash, called Beit El by Jacob, is the destination reached through the Luz pathway. The text states 'through the Luz one enters Beit El' and 'the Beit HaMikdash is the bechina of Beit El.' The Temple represents the same good/holy domain of consolation and divine dwelling that the resurrection/Luz bone promises.
nodes: שלשה שבועות שהם עשרים ואחד יום שבין המצרים

merge_notes.reason: This isolated pair was a separate 2-node component. The proof text establishes that these are bechina of each other — Jacob called the Beit HaMikdash 'Beit El.' The Temple's essential nature in this Torah is as the holy destination of consolation that the Luz-pathway leads to. It belongs thematically with the good/consolation cluster (Package 2) rather than the neutral anatomical cluster (Package 1). The connection is bechina (same sacred place, two names), not eitza.
